posts.title: OpenWorker -- an open source agent that doesn't just chat but completes tasks on your laptop -- just released a new version with many features for security workflows. After our initial release, many users found it especially useful for cybersecurity. Attackers are already using AI; OpenWorker is committed to giving defenders the same leverage. Running an agent requires both (i) A model and (ii) A harness (the software around the model). Because the OpenWorker harness is fully open source, security teams can audit it to make sure we haven't built any backdoors that exfiltrate your code and data to some company or even a foreign adversary. OpenWorker now comes with built-in cybersecurity agents for (i) Scanning your code for vulnerabilities. (ii) Scanning dependencies for supply chain injections. (iii) Checking your cloud security configuration for attack surfaces. This enables developers to do much more security work before deployment (part of what's called the "shift left" movement). You choose the model: you can run open weight models fully locally so sensitive code never leaves your machine. posts.title: Navitas Semiconductor（纳微半导体，NVTS）昨天宣布以最高 2.328 亿美元收购电源管理初创公司 Claros，推动股价盘中大涨近 10%。这笔交易标志着纳微从传统的功率器件供应商，正式向 AI 数据中心全链路供电方案商（Grid-to-xPU） 升级。 当前 AI 芯片（GPU/TPU/ASIC）功耗动辄突破 1000W–2000W，核心电压降至 1V 以下，电流高达数千安培。传统的横向供电（Lateral Power Delivery）因走线阻抗和寄生电感，面临严重的压降（$I^2R$ 损耗）和响应延迟，形成了限制算力释放的「供电墙（Power Wall）」。 垂直供电（VPD）与集成稳压（IVR）： Claros 的核心技术是将功率转换、驱动、控制与无源器件高度集成，直接置于芯片封装底部或基板内部（3D 堆叠）。供电路径从英寸级缩短至毫米级，大幅降低阻抗并提升瞬态响应速度。 打通「电网到算力核心（Grid-to-xPU）」全链路： 纳微原有的 GaN（氮化镓）和 SiC（碳化硅）强在 800V/48V 等高压、高功率转换端；融入 Claros 后，纳微实现了从电网输入、机架级高压配电、板级转换，一直到核心芯片 sub-1V 的全栈电源半导体闭环。 纳微预计，此次收购将直接为其增加至少 35 亿美元的 VPD/IVR 市场空间，使公司 2030 年的可服务市场总规模（SAM）翻倍突破 80 亿美元。 在下一代超大规模数据中心中，超节点（Megawatt Scale）对供电密度要求极高。拥有全链条 IP 的供应商能够提供一体化参考设计，相较单一分立器件厂商具备更强的议价能力与平台壁垒。 收购消息推动今天股价大涨，资本市场的积极反应反映了对「AI 基础设施向电源侧外溢」这一逻辑的高度认可。纳微此举在技术路线上精准卡位了算力芯片的终极供电形态（3D/垂直封装供电）；后续观察重点在于 2026 年底前的交割进展、与头部 GPU/ASIC 厂商的验证定点，以及整体盈利时间表能否如期推进。

posts.title: TrendForce’s supply chain checks indicate that prices for NVIDIA’s server GPUs have remained largely unchanged so far this year. However, rising costs for upstream components such as HBM and wafers, combined with pressure to maintain gross margins, are creating conditions for potential GPU price increases after 1Q27. posts.title: Give every trading tool ONE responsibility: Trend → Moving averages Momentum → MACD Extended → RSI Volatility → ATR Trend strength → ADX Participation → Volume Risk → Position sizing Exit → Stop loss Discipline → Trading Psychology Improving → Trading Journal

A breakout needs context. Breaking above resistance inside a long-term uptrend is one thing. Breaking above yesterday's high inside a major downtrend is another. Same price action. Completely different setup.
Follow the trend. Follow the trend. Follow the trend. Until price proves the trend has changed. Loyalty belongs to your trading process, not your position.
A moving average isn't a prediction. It's a filter. Its job isn't to tell you what happens tomorrow. Its job is to help you determine which side of the trend you're trading today.
You don't need to predict the top. You don't need to predict the bottom. You need a strategy for trading the price action in between those extremes.

Neil shared a cool story of how a skunkworks project turned Nvidia's gaming GPUs into AI chips, starting in 2015: "I remember reading some of the lab notebooks of some of my managers when I was at Nvidia. They would visit these small ML conferences like ICML or NeurIPS at the time, and they would just take note of these papers. "What's really interesting is that these grad students are using gaming Nvidia GPUs in order to train their large models. We should double-click on this and figure out what's going on here." By 2015, 2016, Jensen had the conviction to double down on, "hey, this usage of our chips is only gonna grow. Let's put the first version of tensor cores on the chip." We're talking about taking this gaming chip, which is designed for painting pixels on a screen, and adapting it to do matrix multiplies. It was early, and we would be competing against the graphics teams, essentially. You don't ever want to invest in the wrong technology, because that's opportunity cost that you could have allocated to some other functionality. And so we fought tooth and nail and got just a tiny bit of die area, maybe five, ten percent."

Neil Movva (@neilmovva) started his career at Nvidia, working on GPUs and kernels, and has an unusually deep understanding of inference, from software to chips to power. We spend a lot of time on each of those layers, how they connect, and where the important tradeoffs are. What makes this conversation special is how detailed it is (like a 401-level class), yet Neil makes it remarkably clear and easy to follow. Today he runs Sail Research, a company building infrastructure for agents to make tokens as cheap as possible. We discuss: - Latency versus throughput - Why there are no bad chips, only bad pricing - The end of kernel engineering - Buying chips and power no one else wants - New chip architectures - Nvidia lore + his contrarian view of the company - Open source and the frontier labs I learned a ton. Enjoy!
